chapters.title: Measurements
chapters.slo_codes: No SLO codes printed; 'Learning Objectives' box on opener (PDF 4) with 9 bullets
learning_outcomes: Make reasonable estimates of physical quantities
Differentiate base/derived SI units
Use prefixes and conventions of SI
Analyse homogeneity of physical equations through dimensions
Derive formulas using dimensional analysis
Appreciate that all measurements contain uncertainty
Express uncertainty as absolute/fractional/percentage
Use significant figures in scientific notation
Assess total uncertainty in a final result
Distinguish precision and accuracy
chapters.main_concept: Introduces physical quantities, the SI system (base/derived units, prefixes, writing conventions), uncertainty in measurement (absolute, fractional, percentage), significant figures and rounding rules, precision vs accuracy, propagation of uncertainty in results, and dimensional analysis (homogeneity check and derivation of formulas).

chapters.title: Force and Motion
chapters.slo_codes: No SLO codes printed; 'Learning Objectives' box on opener (PDF 22), ~9 bullets with bracketed sub-notes
learning_outcomes: Differentiate scalar and vector quantities
Represent a vector in 2-D as two perpendicular components
Describe dot and cross product with properties
Derive the equations of motion (uniform acceleration, incl. graphically)
Solve problems using equations of motion (straight line, free fall without air resistance, vertical/horizontal components)
Evaluate and analyse projectile motion (height, range, time of flight, launch angle)
Predict qualitatively how air resistance affects projectile motion
Apply conservation of momentum to elastic and inelastic interactions in 1-D and 2-D (karate chops, car crashes, ball and bat, rocket thrust)
Predict motion for elastic collisions (relative speed of approach = relative speed of separation)
Justify why momentum of a closed system is conserved while KE may change
chapters.main_concept: Builds vector algebra (components, scalar and vector products), derives the three equations of motion algebraically and graphically, applies them to free fall and projectile motion, then develops linear momentum, impulse, conservation of momentum, elastic and inelastic collisions in one and two dimensions, and rocket propulsion.

chapters.title: Circular and Rotational Motion
chapters.slo_codes: No SLO codes printed; 'Learning Objectives' box on opener (PDF 54), 13 bullets
learning_outcomes: Express angles in radians
Define/calculate angular displacement, velocity and acceleration (S = r theta, v = r omega, omega = 2 pi/T, a = v^2/r)
Use equations of angular motion
Discuss motion in a curved path due to a perpendicular force
Define and calculate centripetal force (Fc = m r omega^2 = m v^2/r)
Analyse circular motion where centripetal force is tension, friction, gravity or normal force
Define/calculate orbital speed of a satellite (v = 2 pi r/T)
Explain weightlessness in orbit and artificial gravity
Define/calculate moment of inertia and angular momentum
Derive and apply torque = I alpha; conservation of angular momentum (flywheel, gyroscope, ice skater)
Describe how a centrifuge separates materials
chapters.main_concept: Develops angular kinematics (radian, angular displacement/velocity/acceleration, relation to linear quantities, angular equations of motion), centripetal force and its applications (centrifuge, banked roads), artificial satellites (critical/orbital velocity, weightlessness, artificial gravity), moment of inertia, angular momentum and its conservation with applications (diver, skater, flywheel, gyroscope).

chapters.slo_codes: No SLO codes printed; 'Learning Objectives' box on opener (PDF 93), 19 bullets
learning_outcomes: Distinguish crystalline, amorphous and polymeric solids
Describe one-dimensional deformation (tensile/compressive)

chapters.main_concept: Covers the structure of solids, mechanical properties (stress, strain, Young's modulus, Searle's experiment, stress-strain curve, strain energy), Archimedes' principle and floatation, then fluid dynamics: ideal fluid, rate of flow, equation of continuity, Bernoulli's equation and its applications (aerofoil lift, Magnus effect, filter pump, carburetor, atomizer, Venturi meter, Torricelli's theorem), viscous drag, Stokes' law, terminal velocity, real fluids and superfluids.

chapters.title: Chemical Bonding
chapters.slo_codes: [C-11-A-26 to C-11-A-46] printed p46; 21 SLOs
chapters.main_concept: Lewis view of ionic, covalent and dative bonds and expanded octets, bond polarity and dipole moments from electronegativity, then the three bonding models: VSEPR (AB2-AB6 shapes, drug-design application), valence bond theory with sigma/pi overlap and sp3/sp2/sp hybridization, and molecular orbital theory with MO diagrams and bond orders of He2, N2, O2. Ends with bond energy/length data and a comparison of bond strengths with intermolecular forces.

chapters.title: Molecular Biology (chapter banner printed as 'Biomolecules')
chapters.slo_codes: No SLO codes printed; Students' Learning Outcomes list of 29 bullets (PDF 94)
chapters.main_concept: Surveys the chemistry of life: biological bonds, condensation/hydrolysis, the properties of water, and the structure, classification and roles of carbohydrates, proteins (amino acids to quaternary structure), lipids and nucleic acids (nucleotides, DNA double helix, RNA types, central dogma), ending with conjugated molecules.

chapters.slo_codes: No SLO codes printed; Students' Learning Outcomes list of 14 bullets (PDF 130)

chapters.title: Bioenergetics
chapters.slo_codes: No SLO codes printed; Students' Learning Outcomes list of 21 bullets (PDF 143)
chapters.main_concept: Covers how cells capture and release energy: ATP structure and cycle; photosynthesis (pigments, photosystems, light-dependent non-cyclic/cyclic photophosphorylation with chemiosmosis, Calvin cycle); cellular respiration (anaerobic fermentations; aerobic glycolysis, pyruvate oxidation, Krebs cycle, electron transport chain and chemiosmosis, 36 ATP yield); and photorespiration with the C-4 and CAM adaptations.

Organization of Photosynthetic Pigments (Photosystems): antenna complex, reaction centre, PS-I P700, PS-II P680 (PDF 149-150)

1- Light-Dependent Reactions: a) Non-Cyclic Photophosphorylation (5 steps: absorption by PS-II, photolysis, electron flow PS-II to PS-I via PQ/cytochrome/PC, absorption by PS-I, electron flow to NADP+ via ferredoxin; Z-scheme), b) Cyclic Photophosphorylation, Chemiosmosis (ATP synthase) (PDF 151-153)
2- Light-Independent Reactions (Calvin cycle; Melvin Calvin Nobel 1961): Phase I Carbon Fixation (Rubisco, RuBP, 3-PGA), Phase II Reduction (G3P), Phase III Regeneration of RuBP (PDF 154-155)

Stage 2: Pyruvic acid Oxidation (3 steps; acetyl-CoA) (PDF 159)

chapters.title: Limit and Continuity
chapters.slo_codes: No SLO codes printed; INTRODUCTION paragraph (PDF 223). Opener title 'Limit and Continuity'; TOC 'Limits and Continuity'; running head 'Limit of Sequences and Continuity'.
chapters.main_concept: Builds the idea of a limit (x approaches zero / infinity / a), estimates limits geometrically (inscribed polygons approaching pi) and numerically (tables), states the limit theorems, evaluates standard limits ((x^n - a^n)/(x-a), rational/radical forms, limits at infinity, limits of sequences, (1+1/n)^n = e, (a^x - 1)/x = ln a, sin x/x = 1 via the sandwich theorem), then treats one-sided limits, continuity at a point and real-world limit models.

chapters.title: Vectors in Space
chapters.slo_codes: No SLO codes printed; INTRODUCTION paragraph (PDF 264)
chapters.main_concept: Recalls plane vectors, then builds vectors in 3-D space: rectangular coordinates and the right-hand rule, components with unit vectors i, j, k, magnitude, unit vectors, distance formula, direction angles and cosines. Develops the dot product (projection, orthogonality, angle, work done), the cross product (determinant formula, parallel vectors, area of parallelogram/triangle, moment of force) and the scalar triple product (volume of parallelepiped and tetrahedron, coplanarity), with trigonometric proofs and real-world applications (torque, force magnitude, revenue).
